children: was on track to widen its losses to the seventh straight session on Wednesday, with shares down 3.52% to $12.90.
The stock has been on a downward trajectory since October 6, when it closed 0.62% lower at $14.51. On October 9, it slipped 2.58% to $13.96, dragging the stock further.
Between October 6 and October 13, RIVN lost nearly 8%, compared to a flat S&P500 index.

, Rivian has been rated Hold with a score of 3.16 out of 5. The company has been graded D- for valuation and F for profitability. Wall Street analysts have also echoed similar sentiments and issued a Hold call for the stock. However, Seeking Alpha analysts have rated the stock as Buy.
In an article last week, Seeking Alpha analyst
upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold, noting that the automaker delivered 19,248 EVs in Q3, achieving 45.8% year-over-year growth, driven by strong R2 SUV adoption.
Rivian’s lower-cost R2 launch is accelerating delivery growth, potentially driving analyst estimate upgrades and a strong Q3 earnings report, the analyst said.

“The EV company expects a positive gross margin contribution toward the end of the current fiscal year, which suggests that Rivian could issue an even more attractive growth outlook for next year. Because of the market success with the R2, I am upgrading Rivian from 'Hold' to 'Buy' as execution risks have now been drastically reduced,” it said.

title: Rivian on track to log losses for seventh straight session
